MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 11, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at 5:00
p.m., on March 11, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
p.m. on March 6, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:01 Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  March 11, 2025
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley indicated that the Council was updated, but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Vasquez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim the Month of March 2025 To Be Red Cross Month

  Presented proclamation David Engwall from American Red Cross of Orange County.

P2. Update on Potocki Center for the Arts

  Received presentation by Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen.

Mayor Ruesch asked Chief of Police Jason Ivins to come to the podium to reiterate the Sheriff’s policy
on immigration and the county’s policy on this subject due to questions that arose from the last City
Council Meeting.

Police Chief Ivins read from a press release from Sheriff Barnes dated January 27, 2025.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Madina Kamran, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Community of Character and announced the character
word of the month is Integrity.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked the City Council how they plan to stagger the terms for the 2026 and 2028
elections and asked that this be addressed at a future meeting.

Kristen Wilcox, M.V.: Asked that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids be put on the next
City Council agenda and asked that the City declare itself as a Sanctuary City. She also asked that the
Council publicly disclose the plans for the next election pertaining to the staggering of districts.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke on the three-minute public comment time limit and asked that the same be
followed by the council members per their council policy.

Tony Dorta, M.V.: Voiced concerns on commercial vans parking on Athens Court and the lack of
visibility for residents trying to make a left or right from San Remo Place. He asked that the Council
look into this and perhaps install “no parking” signs.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item #17 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

City Council Minutes  2  March 11, 2025
 Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  March 11, 2025
 10. Single Audit Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024

  Received and filed.

11. Designation of Positions as Authorized Agents to Apply for Federal and State Financial

  Adopted Resolution 25-05 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents for the Purpose of
  Obtaining Federal Financial Assistance and/or State Financial Assistance for Federal Fiscal Years

  (1) Approved Fifth Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services with BPR, Inc., for

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

17. Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract 2025-2027

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract for 2025-2027 (A25-05) in
  the amount of $134,596 in FY 2025-2026 and $151,874 in 2026-2027 as recommended by the
  Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  March 11, 2025
 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

21. New Commercial Development Proposals and New Commercial Businesses Update

  Received update from Director of Community Development Larry Longenecker.

22. Federal and State Grant Update

  Received update from City Manager Lister.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell clarified for the record that Council Member Kelley and himself forfeited two
years of their terms so that all five members could run together in order to implement district-wide
voting. He attended the Chamber of Commerce’s mixer and the amazing tour of the Leonard Cancer
Institute at Mission Hospital. He encouraged residents to take the tour of that facility. They have some
of the most technically advanced laser methods for treating cancer. Council member Goodell also
attended the Jeff Lauder Celebration of Life. Jeff was one of the founders of Mission Viejo. He
announced that he rejoined the South Orange County Executive Watershed Management Committee.
Lastly, he announced that the O’Neill family are the ones who donated the land for Mission Hospital
and continue their stewardship of this community with a fifty-million-dollar donation.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley participated in reading at two elementary schools this past week. She stated at
her recent Orange County Division of the League of California Cities meeting that State Senator Stephen
Choi spoke on the importance of local control and talked about various pieces of legislation that we
support and asked for his endorsement on these issues. Council Member Kelley along with several other
council members attended the North Mission Viejo and South Mission Viejo Little League Opening
Day Ceremonies. She attended a ribbon cutting ceremony with Mayor Ruesch for Marque Urgent Care
Center in the Olympia Plaza Center. Council Member Kelley attended the Meet the Mayors in Laguna
Niguel and commended Mayor Ruesch for his nice overview of the sports tourism focus that Mission
Viejo is relying on at this time. She also attended the Conrad Reuland Fundraiser and gave kudos to
staff. She also commented on the hospital expansion and the donation from the O’Neill family. Council
Member Kelley stated that she attended the Persian New Year Event at Newhart Middle School and got
to sample some of the food. Lastly, she mentioned that The Red Cross blood drives will no longer be
holding blood drives in their trailers and is in need of new locations and that they are in need of blood.

City Council Minutes  6  March 11, 2025
 Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez asked specifically for clarification as to what Mission Viejo’s position is on
ICE. Chief Ivins explained that we abide by SB54 and have limited communication with ICE. She
attended Read Across America at Bathgate Elementary School and read to her daughter’s third grade
class. She attended the Conrad Reuland Fundraiser and was very impressed with the turnout and all the
items one could bid on. Council Member Vasquez also attended the first of the free concert series at
Norman P. Community Center last week and really enjoyed the band. Lastly, she mentioned that her
Girl Scout Troop is kicking off a crayon drive, so if you have any crayons, she will be happy to recycle
them so that the troop may donate to an organization called The Crayon Initiative. The Crayon Initiative
melts all the crayons and makes new ones to provide packages of crayons to children in children’s
hospitals all over the United States.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum commented on an earlier public comment regarding ICE. She stated that
Mission Viejo residents have suffered from some crime at the hands of international gangs and these
people should not be in our Country, let alone our City and we should not get in the way of people like
that being brought to justice. She also stated that we should not be a sanctuary city and from her seat
she would never vote for that. She also attended Jeff Lauder’s celebration of life and said there was a
lot of history told, and it was a very nice celebration. Mayor Pro Tem also attended the Meet the Mayor
event in Laguna Niguel and complimented Mayor Ruesch on his speech. She also attended the Conrad
Reuland Charity Event and stated it is great to see how this event has grown over the years. She attended
the dedication at Providence Mission Hospital and stated it was very meaningful to her and recognized
the many attributes Tony Moiso and family have given to our community. Lastly, she reminded residents
that this Saturday is the St. Patrick’s Day Night Market and encouraged everyone to attend along with
the Farmers Market in the morning.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch told the public that the Council is very active and takes an interest in our city affairs by
participating in all the events in our city. He thanked his council colleagues for representing the city and
attending the hospital tour as he was unable to due to an Orange County Fire Authority emergency
meeting and a personal appointment he could not get out of. He also participated in Read Across
America at Bathgate Elementary School for Mrs. Anderson’s fifth grade class and received thank you
cards from the students. Mayor Ruesch participated in the Meet the Mayors and stated there is a lot of
interest in our City from other surrounding cities and is happy to be representing Mission Viejo and the
connections that have been made with all of South Orange County, as well as North Orange County. He
attended the opening day of Mission Viejo Yacht Club along with approximately seventy-five others,
which was a fantastic event. Lastly, he adjourned the meeting with the following words, “Whatever
good things we build end up building us”.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:26 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 25, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.
